name: Stipple ramp
sub: Tone made of whole pen dots. Value sets how many sites print (FM) or how big each dot is (AM); a blue-noise rank picks the sites. Each dot is crisp geometry whose edge the stock's tooth nudges — never softened.

in.o: params object — keys below; every length in CSS px
in.dpr: device px per CSS px (density is physical: marks per CSS px²)

x.S: params of every effect keyed by id; the stock this prints on is read from S[printsOn]
x.umask: optional: clips.umask — a typed or image mask (mShape type | image)

out.lin: Float32Array W·H·3, linear-light sRGB (encode with FX.toRGBA(R,"image",W,H))
out.ink: Float32Array W·H, absorbance / coverage (FX.toRGBA(R,"ink",…) = film positive)
out.stock: Float32Array W·H, stock height (FX.toRGBA(R,"stock",…) = normalized height map)

light.note: az = direction the light comes FROM (screen degrees; 0 = right, 90 = below); el = elevation above the sheet

deterministic: yes — every random draw is a hash of (position, seed); same inputs → same pixels in the same engine

recipe: Site lattice at the pitch (CSS px), jittered. Value field (linear · radial · noise) eased from → to.
Screen: FM keeps a site when its blue-noise rank < value; AM keeps every site with radius ∝ √value; the dial interpolates. The mask is sampled at the site — dots are whole or absent.
Each dot is geometry: a signed distance to an irregular nib outline (7 vertex radii), so its edge is always 1 device px of anti-aliasing — never a blur.
The stock edits the edge: the distance is displaced by the stock height (edge rag), valleys inside the dot can starve, fibers wick a short way out. Film τ = thickness × pressure.
Color: Beer–Lambert film in linear light (or a coverage mix). Ink B overprints by the same film product.
Light last: × the stock's shading under the sheet light.

limits.what: sites merge into flat tone at 1× — the stipple stops reading as marks
below ~½ device px at 1× a dot is a gray pixel, not a mark
dots fuse into a solid; FM loses its range
dots read as fuzz, not ink
clumps and voids at low density
